chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jarir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How much shall I oil (my body)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Once during every year.' So I said, 'Then the people would look at me as a destitute.' So I did not cease bargaining with him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'So in every month, once,' and he (peace be upon him) did not increase over it.

key_terms.أَدَّهِنُ: I oil / I apply oil (from the root دهن, referring to ritual or cosmetic oiling)
key_terms.أُمَاكِسُهُ: I bargain with him / I negotiate with him

ai.seo_question: How often should one oil or massage their body according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the fiqh of *idhān* (anointing with oil), balancing ritual purity with social perception (*mashhūr*). The Imam’s negotiation with the questioner illustrates the principle of *mukāsah* (bargaining in jurisprudence), where the ruling is adjusted to prevent the appearance of poverty or neglect, thereby maintaining dignity while fulfilling the recommended act.
